vaginal process of sphenoid bone: Thin process on the lower surface of the body; articulates with the vomer.
vastus intermedius muscle: Deep head of quadriceps beneath rectus femoris, arising from the front of the femur.
vastus lateralis muscle: The largest head of quadriceps; forms the lateral part of the thigh and is used for intramuscular injections.
vastus medialis muscle: Medial head of quadriceps; its lower oblique fibres (VMO) pull the patella medially and prevent lateral dislocation.
ventral parts of lateral intertransversa: Ventral parts of lateral lumbar intertransversarii
Anterior fibres of the small muscles between the lumbar transverse processes.
vermian fossa: Fossa seen in some people at the lower end of the internal occipital crest; the vermis of the cerebellum lies in it.
vertebra: Bone of the spine; made up of a body and an arch.
vertebra c3: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process.
vertebra c4: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process.
vertebra c5: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process.
vertebra c6: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process. Its anterior tubercle (carotid tubercle) is the point against which the common carotid artery can be compressed.
vertebra c7: Typical cervical vertebra: small body, triangular vertebral foramen, foramen transversarium in the transverse processes and a bifid spinous process. Its spinous process (vertebra prominens) is the first prominent bump felt at the base of the neck; the vertebral artery usually does not pass through its foramen transversarium.
vertebra l1: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes. The spinal cord usually ends at the conus medullaris at the L1–L2 level.
vertebra l2: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes.
vertebra l3: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes.
vertebra l4: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes. The line joining the highest points of the iliac crests (Tuffier's line) usually crosses the L4 spine; the reference for lumbar puncture.
vertebra l5: Lumbar vertebra: large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, quadrilateral spinous process; its processes carry mammillary and accessory processes. The largest vertebra; its body is taller in front (wedge-shaped) and forms the lumbosacral angle with the sacrum. Spondylolisthesis is most common at L5–S1.
vertebra t1: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards. Its body has a whole facet for the 1st rib and a half facet for the 2nd rib.
vertebra t10: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards. It usually carries only a single facet for the 10th rib.
vertebra t11: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards. It has a single rib facet; there is no facet on its transverse process.
vertebra t12: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards. Its body resembles a lumbar vertebra; one of the vertebrae most often fractured at the thoracolumbar junction.
vertebra t2: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards.
vertebra t3: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards.
vertebra t4: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards.
vertebra t5: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards.
vertebra t6: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards.
vertebra t7: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards.
vertebra t8: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards.
vertebra t9: Thoracic vertebra: its body and transverse process carry facets for the ribs, and its spinous process is long and slopes downwards.
vertebral arch: Arch surrounding the vertebral foramen from behind; made up of the pedicles and laminae.
vertebral foramen: Opening surrounded by the body and arch; it contains the spinal cord and its membranes.
vestibular surface of tooth: Surface of a tooth facing the cheek or lip.
vocal process: Forward-projecting process of the arytenoid; the vocal ligament attaches to it.
vomer: Thin single bone forming the posteroinferior part of the nasal septum.
xiphoid process: Lowest, cartilaginous-to-bony tip of the sternum; it gives attachment to the diaphragm and the rectus sheath, and lies below the compression area during CPR.
zona orbicularis: Circular capsular fibres encircling the femoral neck like a ring.
zygomatic bone: Bone forming the prominence of the cheek and the lateral wall of the orbit; with the temporal bone it forms the zygomatic arch.
zygomatic margin of greater wing: Margin that articulates with the zygomatic bone.
zygomatic process of frontal bone: Lateral process that articulates with the zygomatic bone; it forms the upper lateral margin of the orbit.
zygomaticus major muscle: The 'smiling muscle', running from the zygomatic bone to the corner of the mouth; pulls the corner of the mouth up and out.
zygomaticus minor muscle: Raises the upper lip and deepens the nasolabial fold.
